references.text: The men of Ephraim showed the same complaining attitude toward Jephthah as they had shown toward Gideon, accusing him of not calling them to battle.
Gideon had actually called Ephraim to help by taking the fords across the Jordan, so their complaint was unjustified.
Joshua 17 describes Ephraim's territory and the tribe's self-awareness, which explains their pride and sensitivity to being overlooked.
The prophecy about tension between Ephraim and Judah reflects tribal conflicts like the one shown in this text.
A soft answer turns away wrath - Gideon's diplomatic response in verses 2-3 illustrates this principle from Proverbs.
